panels.title: Running containers
panels.description: Containers currently running, per the OrbStack Docker engine.

targets.query:
from(bucket: "system")
  |> range(start: -15m)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "docker" and r._field == "n_containers_running")
  |> last()

from(bucket: "system")
  |> range(start: -15m)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "docker" and r._field == "n_containers")
  |> last()

panels.title: Images
panels.description: Local images in the OrbStack engine. Watch for creep — a weekly prune LaunchAgent trims unused ones.

targets.query:
from(bucket: "system")
  |> range(start: -15m)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "docker" and r._field == "n_images")
  |> last()

panels.title: VM memory limit
panels.description: Total memory the OrbStack Linux VM exposes to the engine (the VM cap — 4 GiB on this 8 GB Mac mini).

targets.query:
from(bucket: "system")
  |> range(start: -15m)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "docker" and r._field == "memory_total")
  |> last()

panels.title: Memory map — container usage (btop-style)
panels.description: Each tile is a container; area ∝ memory used, colour = % of its mem_limit (green → red). A red tile is near its cap and at OOM risk — exactly what the OOM alert fires on.

targets.query:
from(bucket: "system")
  |> range(start: -5m)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "docker_container_mem" and (r._field == "usage" or r._field == "usage_percent" or r._field == "limit"))
  |> last()
  |> pivot(rowKey: ["container_name"], columnKey: ["_field"], valueColumn: "_value")
  |> map(fn: (r) => ({ container_name: r.container_name, usage_mb: float(v: r.usage) / 1048576.0, pct: r.usage_percent, limit_mb: float(v: r.limit) / 1048576.0 }))
  |> filter(fn: (r) => exists r.usage_mb)
  |> keep(columns: ["container_name", "usage_mb", "pct", "limit_mb"])
  |> group()
  |> sort(columns: ["usage_mb"], desc: true)

panels.title: CPU usage % per container
panels.description: docker stats-style CPU percent (relative to total VM CPU; can exceed 100% across cores). Each container is capped at 2 vCPU (50% of the 4-core VM).

targets.query:
from(bucket: "system")
  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "docker_container_cpu" and r._field == "usage_percent")
  |> group(columns: ["container_name"])
  |> aggregateWindow(every: v.windowPeriod, fn: mean, createEmpty: false)
  |> keep(columns: ["_time", "_value", "container_name"])

from(bucket: "system")
  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "docker_container_mem" and r._field == "usage")
  |> group(columns: ["container_name"])
  |> aggregateWindow(every: v.windowPeriod, fn: mean, createEmpty: false)
  |> keep(columns: ["_time", "_value", "container_name"])

panels.title: Memory % of limit per container
panels.description: Container memory as a percent of its mem_limit (2048 MiB cap). Yellow ≥80%, red ≥95% — sustained red means it will soon be OOM-killed by Docker (the intended blast-radius cap, not a VM-wide thrash).

targets.query:
from(bucket: "system")
  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "docker_container_mem" and r._field == "usage_percent")
  |> group(columns: ["container_name"])
  |> aggregateWindow(every: v.windowPeriod, fn: mean, createEmpty: false)
  |> keep(columns: ["_time", "_value", "container_name"])

panels.title: Network I/O per container
panels.description: Per-container network throughput (rate of rx/tx bytes, total across interfaces).

targets.query:
from(bucket: "system")
  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "docker_container_net" and (r._field == "rx_bytes" or r._field == "tx_bytes"))
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r.network == "total")
  |> group(columns: ["container_name", "_field"])
  |> aggregateWindow(every: v.windowPeriod, fn: last, createEmpty: false)
  |> derivative(unit: 1s, nonNegative: true)
  |> keep(columns: ["_time", "_value", "container_name", "_field"])

panels.title: Block I/O per container
panels.description: Per-container disk read/write throughput (rate of blkio bytes, total device). Heavy sustained I/O here is the class of activity that hung the VM on 2026-05-31.

targets.query:
from(bucket: "system")
  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "docker_container_blkio" and (r._field == "io_service_bytes_recursive_read" or r._field == "io_service_bytes_recursive_write"))
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r.device == "total")
  |> group(columns: ["container_name", "_field"])
  |> aggregateWindow(every: v.windowPeriod, fn: last, createEmpty: false)
  |> derivative(unit: 1s, nonNegative: true)
  |> keep(columns: ["_time", "_value", "container_name", "_field"])

panels.title: Container status
panels.description: Latest state per container: status, restart count, last exit code, OOM-killed flag, and uptime. Non-zero restart counts / exit codes flag the kind of crash loop seen with transit-tracker.

targets.query:
from(bucket: "system")
  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "docker_container_status")
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._field == "restart_count" or r._field == "exitcode" or r._field == "oomkilled" or r._field == "uptime_ns")
  |> last()
  |> pivot(rowKey: ["container_name", "container_status", "container_image"], columnKey: ["_field"], valueColumn: "_value")
  |> keep(columns: ["container_name", "container_status", "container_image", "restart_count", "exitcode", "oomkilled", "uptime_ns"])
  |> sort(columns: ["container_name"])
